stories.headline: Canada and China expand trade pact with tariff relief for agriculture and metals
stories.summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney and Chinese President Xi Jinping reached an agreement at the APEC summit to lower tariffs on Canadian pork and seafood in exchange for Canadian tariff concessions on Chinese steel and aluminum. The deal delivers approximately $400 million in export relief for Canadian producers as Ottawa pursues a trade reset following years of strained relations. However, critics and security analysts caution that the economic concessions risk compromising broader geopolitical interests and complicating ties with the United States.

stories.headline: Carney meets Trump in China as Canada-U.S. trade negotiations intensify
stories.summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney held a 20-minute bilateral meeting with U.S. President Donald Trump on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen, China. Carney asserted that Canada's expanding trade ties with China do not threaten Washington, noting Canadian exports to China focus on commodities rather than sensitive technology. The summit discussion comes as senior Canadian and American trade officials ramp up formal weekly negotiations amid friction over U.S. tariffs.

stories.headline: Canada and India close to finalizing bilateral free trade agreement, envoy says
stories.summary: India's high commissioner to Canada announced that Ottawa and New Delhi are on the verge of concluding a comprehensive free trade deal, culminating negotiations that began 16 years ago. In addition to trade terms, the envoy indicated that a bilateral defence agreement is expected to be signed during Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi's planned visit to Ottawa in December. The anticipated deals signal a major diplomatic and commercial rapprochement between the two nations following years of friction.

stories.headline: Federal debt charges are Ottawa's fastest-growing expense, budget watchdog reports
stories.summary: Parliamentary Budget Officer Annette Ryan warned that public debt charges have become the federal government's fastest-growing expenditure following $331.6 billion in new spending measures. The watchdog found that Ottawa has committed 96 percent of its newly gained fiscal room, leaving deficits little changed and reserves nearly exhausted. The report also cautioned that substantial federal borrowing extends well beyond the projected headline deficit.

stories.headline: Federal bill amending medical assistance in dying laws advances amid opposition pushback
stories.summary: The federal Liberal government's proposed legislation amending Canada's medical assistance in dying laws passed second reading in the House of Commons and was referred to the justice committee. Opposition parties objected after the government moved to limit parliamentary debate, demanding additional time to examine safeguards and legal implications. The committee review will examine controversial provisions before the bill returns to the House for final reading.

stories.headline: Experts urge Ottawa to launch national security review of proposed Moneris acquisition
stories.summary: National security experts and economists are urging the federal government to subject the planned takeover of Moneris by a U.S. private equity firm to an exhaustive national security review. Experts warned that handing Canada's largest payment processor to foreign owners jeopardizes domestic financial data sovereignty. Critics also pointed to the acquiring firm's purported ties to international human rights concerns as grounds for ministerial intervention.

articles.author: Robert Fife
articles.title: Ottawa should conduct national security review of Moneris takeover deal, experts say

stories.headline: Ottawa remains noncommittal as Quebecor makes takeover bid for rival Telus
stories.summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney declined to state whether the federal government would permit the telecom industry to lose a major national player following Quebecor's bid to acquire Telus. While the prime minister stressed that Ottawa's priority is fostering competition and lowering consumer prices, analysts note the takeover could create the largest telecommunications firm in Canada. The transaction will face intense scrutiny by federal competition and telecommunications regulators before any approval can be granted.

stories.headline: Ontario English public high school teachers vote overwhelmingly for strike mandate
stories.summary: Members of the Ontario Secondary School Teachers' Federation voted 96 per cent in favour of a strike mandate, increasing pressure on the provincial government. The union cited worsening classroom conditions, growing class sizes, and declining student supports as primary grievances across all five major education unions currently working without contracts. Education Minister Paul Calandra downplayed the outcome, stating that high strike-vote margins are typical during contract negotiations.

stories.headline: Doug Ford pitches Ontario-Quebec economic coalition to counter American trade protectionism
stories.summary: In a speech to the Chamber of Commerce of Metropolitan Montreal, Ontario Premier Doug Ford called for tearing down internal trade barriers and creating a united economic front between Ontario and Quebec. Ford argued that Canada's two largest provinces must coordinate industrial strategies and economic partnerships to weather escalating trade turbulence with the United States. He emphasized that interprovincial collaboration is essential to protecting domestic manufacturing and critical supply chains.

stories.headline: Ontario tables legislation shielding government from lawsuits over private career college OSAP pause
stories.summary: The Ontario government has introduced legislation to protect itself from legal liability resulting from its provincewide suspension of Ontario Student Assistance Program funding to private career colleges. Meanwhile, students enrolled in affected institutions like Trillium College have voiced outrage after schools allowed only students capable of paying out of pocket to continue coursework. The measure shields the province from damages as it reviews funding integrity across private post-secondary institutions.

stories.headline: Ontario NDP requests Elections Ontario investigation into Progressive Conservative fundraising
stories.summary: The Ontario NDP has formally asked Elections Ontario to review bank deposit records to determine whether the governing Progressive Conservatives accepted illegal political donations. The complaint follows reports that the Ford government pledged $175 million to the horse racing industry shortly after a cabinet minister raised $20,000 from sector executives. The opposition alleges a pattern of access-for-donations fundraising that compromises public procurement and subsidy decisions.

stories.headline: Ontario to introduce legislation hiking fines for loud mufflers and excessive vehicle noise
stories.summary: The Ontario government plans to introduce legislation that significantly increases minimum fines for drivers operating vehicles with excessively loud engine revving or illegal exhaust modifications. Provincial officials aim to clamp down on street racing and nuisance noise in urban neighbourhoods across the province. The bill will establish tougher statutory penalties for motorists and mechanics who tamper with vehicle noise-dampening systems.

articles.author: Meredith Bond
articles.title: Ford government moves to silence loud car and truck noise with new legislation

stories.headline: Real estate developers challenge Mississauga's data centre moratorium at provincial tribunal
stories.summary: U.S. industrial real estate giant Prologis and Toronto firm Montcrest Asset Management have appealed Mississauga's one-year freeze on data centres over 10 megawatts to the Ontario Land Tribunal. City council enacted the pause to evaluate power grid capacity, land-use zoning, and noise concerns associated with power-hungry facilities. Mississauga's mayor welcomed the legal fight, declaring the city is ready to defend its planning authority.

stories.headline: Toronto City Council convenes new term with seven new members and housing priorities
stories.summary: Mayor Olivia Chow and 25 city councillors were sworn in for the new term, marking the arrival of seven new council members, including former federal MPs Nate Erskine-Smith and Shaun Chen. Several incoming councillors with backgrounds in grassroots housing advocacy intend to prioritize tenant protections and homelessness solutions on the council floor. Chow delivered her inaugural address outlining her administration's agenda, working with a council expected to be more ideologically aligned with her priorities.

stories.headline: TTC transit union urges board to act promptly over misconduct allegations against CEO
stories.summary: The transit union representing TTC frontline workers has called on the transit agency's board of directors to act swiftly and maintain transparency regarding workplace misconduct investigations involving CEO Mandeep Lali. The union emphasized that senior transit leadership must be held to the highest standards of workplace accountability. The TTC board has not yet issued formal public findings on the internal investigation.
